issues.body: `_via_app_proof` accepts every non-boolean Python integer as an App identity. Thus `performed_via_github_app: {"id": 0}` and `{"id": -1}` return true even when no usable slug exists. Neither value can identify a real GitHub App, but `label_owner_from_events` consequently returns `LABEL_OWNER_MACHINE`, and the boolean projection authorizes deletion. This is the same trust-direction defect as round 1 in a narrower shape: malformed metadata is still accepted as positive automation proof. The new malformed-object table omits both boundary values, so it cannot catch this permissive predicate.
issues.fix_hint: Require an integer App id to be strictly positive (while continuing to exclude booleans), unless a separately valid non-blank slug supplies the identity. Add red tests for objects containing only `id: 0` and only a negative id through both the pure ownership walk and the absorbing/clearability wrapper; they must raise or resolve conservatively, never produce MACHINE. Retain positive-id and slug-only acceptance tests.
issues.title: Non-positive App IDs still mint machine ownership

verdict.summary: The round-1 failure is narrowed but not closed. The new helper rejects many malformed App-marker shapes and the added tests exercise those cases, but its integer-id branch still treats zero and negative integers as attributable GitHub App identities. Those values cannot identify a real App, yet they produce MACHINE and therefore permission to delete a hold. Because the same positive-proof boundary remains fail-open for malformed metadata, progress is stagnant.
